finding.claim: Stored, unvalidated callback URLs are POSTed to by the server every minute, allowing requests to arbitrary internal or external hosts such as localhost, the cloud metadata address 169.254.169.254, or RFC1918 services.
finding.source: callbackUrl parameter of Jobs.subscribe at src/Jobs.java:13, taken from the POST /subscribe request body per the comment at src/Jobs.java:12. The route and its auth are not in this repo.
finding.sink: client.send(req, ...) at src/Jobs.java:24, with the URI built by URI.create(cb) at src/Jobs.java:21.

trace.note: Comment documents POST /subscribe with name and callbackUrl in the body.
subscribe() accepts callbackUrl as a raw String.
callbackUrl is stored in the static subscriptions map without parsing, scheme, host, or allowlist checks.
notifyAll(payload) runs on a schedule per the comment at line 17.
Iterates over every stored callback URL.
Each stored string goes to URI.create with no validation.
Request is a POST whose body is the payload argument.

client.send issues the outbound request from the server. The response body is discarded, so the attacker gets no response content, but side effects, port and host probing, and exfiltration of payload to the attacker host remain.

finding.guards_checked: No null or empty check, no scheme restriction (http and https are both allowed), no host or IP allowlist, no blocking of loopback, link-local, or private addresses, no port restriction, no DNS check. The client at src/Jobs.java:10 uses default settings, which do not follow redirects, so redirect-based bypass is not possible, but the initial target is unrestricted. Exploitability depends on whether POST /subscribe is reachable by untrusted users and on what payload notifyAll receives, neither of which is visible in this repo.

verdict.guard_found: none: src/Jobs.java:14 stores callbackUrl unvalidated, and src/Jobs.java:21 passes it straight to URI.create with no scheme, host, or IP check. The only validation in the file is the regex at src/Jobs.java:30, which guards thumb() and not notifyAll().
verdict.reason: Every trace line checks out (src/Jobs.java:12-24), and no guard closes the path, but whether callbackUrl is attacker-controlled depends on the POST /subscribe route at src/Jobs.java:12, which is not in this repo, so its reachability and authentication cannot be confirmed here.
